newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arab League says U.N. backs Palestinians.
newsitem.headline: Arab League says U.N. backs Palestinians.

text.p: The Arab League on Sunday welcomed the U.N. Security Council resolution passed in reaction to clashes between Palestinians and Israeli troops.

A spokesman for the Cairo-based league called on hardline Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to immediately close the controversial archaeological tunnel near the al-Aqsa mosque, Islam's third holiest site.
Fifty-five Palestinians and 14 Israeli soldiers have died in clashes since Israel opened a new entrance to the tunnel.

"The U.N. Security Council resolution affirms that world opinion stands against Israel's inhuman practices towards the Palestinian people and Islamic and Christian holy sites," Arab League spokesman Talaat Hamed told Reuters.

The United States was the lone absention on Saturday when the 14 other members of the Security Council called for ensuring the safety of Palestinian civilians and for the immediate resumption of the peace talks.

"The statements of the delegations to the Security Council clearly stated that the practices of Netanyahu's government are turning the clock back and are placing the Middle East on the edge of the abyss," Hamed said.

"This necessitates immediate and serious movement by the international community to make Israel implement what has been decided by international law and what it agreed upon with the parties in the peace process.
"Events require that redeployment from Hebron must take place quickly and the tunnel must be closed as a sign of good faith and as a start towards resuming peace talks," he added.
Israeli troops were supposed to redeploy from Hebron earlier this year under an agreement reached with the Palestinians but Israel has delayed the withdrawal for security reasons.
The U.N. resolution did not specifically criticise Israel, but it implicitly called for closing the tunnel entrance and contained other elements to which Israel objected.
Hamed said the United States abstained from the vote because "it is on the verge of an election battle in which the Jewish lobby plays an effective role.
